evidence_items.content: Concept drift refers to an online supervised-learning setting in which the relationship between input data and the target variable changes over time; adaptation methods therefore address changing predictive relationships rather than prediction-error magnitude alone.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Defines the semantic condition that distinguishes relationship change from a generic increase in observed error.

evidence_items.content: Adaptive data-driven soft-sensor methods can be classified into moving-window, recursive-adaptation, and ensemble-based approaches. The review treats concept drift as a model-maintenance problem and shows that adaptation is not restricted to complete replacement or retraining of the base model.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Shows that model maintenance has multiple adaptation levels, so full base-model retraining is not the default response to every degradation signal.

evidence_items.content: An industrial soft-sensor maintenance method used a Kalman-filter-based model-mismatch index together with T² and SPE process-monitoring indices to monitor prediction performance and guide model-update timing; the subsequent PLS update incorporated new process-condition samples.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Provides industrial evidence that update timing can be based on persistent model mismatch together with process-state monitoring rather than error magnitude alone.

evidence_items.content: For production ML systems, testing and monitoring are central to production readiness and technical-debt reduction; the paper presents 28 concrete tests and monitoring needs derived from production experience, supporting explicit monitoring before maintenance actions are automated.
evidence_items.selection_reason: Supports treating retraining as a monitored lifecycle action rather than a reflexive response to a single metric excursion.
